paperMetadata.title: Towards Better Code Generation and Program Synthesis: An Empirical Analysis

abstract: In recent years, code generation and program synthesis have garnered attention with the emergence of models capable of translating natural language into executable code. However, challenges persist in achieving high accuracy, multi-language support, and robust execution-based evaluation. This paper introduces a novel model that integrates retrieval-augmented generation with a self-debugging mechanism to improve code generation tasks. Our approach leverages a dual-encoder architecture to retrieve relevant code snippets, which are then refined through a transformer-based generator augmented with execution feedback loops. We validate the efficacy of our method on tasks including code completion, bug fixing, and code translation across multiple programming languages. Our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with a 15% increase in accuracy on average. The primary contributions of this work include a novel retrieval-augmented architecture, a self-debugging mechanism that iteratively refines outputs, and comprehensive evaluation across multiple code synthesis tasks.

contributions.title: Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
contributions.description: We propose a novel retrieval-augmented model that incorporates a dual-encoder architecture to leverage existing code repositories effectively. By retrieving relevant code snippets, the model enhances the contextual understanding necessary for accurate code generation.
contributions.novelty: This approach is innovative in combining retrieval mechanisms with traditional transformer-based generation, thus improving accuracy and context relevance in code synthesis.

contributions.title: Self-Debugging Mechanism
contributions.description: The self-debugging mechanism refines generated code by executing and analyzing errors, iteratively improving the output. This feedback loop helps the model learn from its mistakes, leading to more robust code generation.
contributions.novelty: Unlike previous works, our method incorporates execution-based feedback directly into the generation process, enhancing reliability and correctness.

contributions.title: Comprehensive Multi-Language Support
contributions.description: Our model supports code generation across multiple programming languages, making it versatile for various applications. This is achieved through a language-agnostic encoder and a language-specific decoder.
contributions.novelty: This contribution addresses the challenge of multi-language support in program synthesis, providing a unified framework that adapts to different programming languages.

methodology.problemFormulation: The task is to generate executable code snippets from natural language descriptions, focusing on improving accuracy, language diversity, and execution validation.
methodology.approach: We employ a dual-encoder architecture for retrieval-augmented generation, coupled with a transformer-based generator. The model includes a self-debugging component that iteratively refines code by executing and analyzing errors.

components.name: Dual-Encoder
components.role: Retrieves relevant code snippets from a database to enhance contextual understanding.
components.details: The dual-encoder consists of a query encoder and a code encoder, both based on transformer architectures, enabling efficient retrieval of contextually similar code.

components.name: Transformer-Based Generator
components.role: Generates the initial code snippet based on retrieved context.
components.details: Utilizes a standard transformer decoder architecture with attention mechanisms to produce code from the combined natural language and retrieved context.

components.name: Self-Debugger
components.role: Refines generated code by executing it and learning from errors.
components.details: Implements execution-based evaluation, analyzing stack traces and error logs to iteratively improve the code generation process.

assumptions: Assume access to a large, diverse code repository for retrieval.
Assume error logs and stack traces provide sufficient information for debugging.
limitations: The model's performance depends heavily on the quality of the code repository.
Execution-based feedback may be limited by the computational resources available for code execution.

evidence.description: Validate the model's performance on code completion tasks.

setup.context: Evaluate using a benchmark dataset of code completion tasks in Python and Java.
conditions: Baseline models include GPT-3 and Codex.

evaluation.protocol: Compare model outputs to ground truth and measure execution success.

evidence.analysis: The model significantly improves code completion accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of retrieval-augmented generation and self-debugging in practical scenarios.

works.summary: Introduced the transformer architecture, laying the foundation for subsequent code generation models.
Explored execution-based metrics as a means of evaluating code generation accuracy.
Investigated models capable of translating code between multiple programming languages.
Developed systems that learn from execution errors to improve performance over time.

futureWork.direction: Enhancing Code Retrieval with Semantic Search
futureWork.motivation: To improve the relevance of retrieved code snippets, integrating semantic search techniques will be explored to better capture the intent behind natural language queries.
To further enhance the model's utility, expanding support to additional programming languages will address the diversity of programming environments in real-world applications.
